title: FY2003 spans the creation of ICE
text: ICE began operating on March 1, 2003, partway through fiscal year 2003 (Oct 2002–Sep 2003). ICE's FY2003 figure is the first it publishes; the months before March were carried out by the former INS and the Customs Service. Treat FY2003 as a part-year ICE count. (General knowledge — not stated in the snapshot.)

title: Removals only — returns not included
text: ICE states that its removal data include returns starting in FY2007. FY2003–FY2006 are therefore removals only, and FY2007's jump over FY2006 is partly a change in what is counted, not only in enforcement. Do not read the FY2006→FY2007 step as a like-for-like change.

title: “Removals” include returns
text: From FY2007 ICE's removal count includes returns — voluntary returns, voluntary departures and withdrawals under docket control — in addition to removals under an order of removal. ICE's own definition (dashboard glossary, FY2024 annual report) still says so. Compare with DHS or OHSS series that count removals alone and the numbers will differ.

title: Counts are locked on October 5; later closures roll into the next year
text: Since FY2009 ICE locks each year's statistics around October 5 and counts only removals or returns already confirmed. Departures confirmed after that date are counted in the following fiscal year, so a year's figure can include some prior-year departures ('lag'). ICE publishes alternate 'excluding lag' totals for some years (for example FY2013: 363,144); this series always uses ICE's headline, as-locked figure.

title: FY2010 excludes 76,732 CBP expedited removals
text: ICE notes that its FY2010 figure does not include 76,732 expedited-removal cases ICE closed on behalf of CBP (33,900 from a joint CBP/ICE operation in Arizona).

title: From June 1, 2013, un-detained expedited removals and voluntary returns are not ICE removals
text: ICE counts expedited removals and voluntary returns only when ICE took the person into custody (an ICE intake). Voluntary returns recorded on or after June 1, 2013 without an ICE intake are not recorded as ICE removals; those are processed mainly by Border Patrol and published by CBP.

title: Title 42 expulsions are not removals
text: From March 2020 until May 11, 2023, many border crossers were expelled under Title 42 (public-health authority) rather than removed under Title 8. ICE excludes expulsions from its removal count (62,545 in FY2023 alone), which depresses FY2020–FY2023 relative to earlier years.

title: FY2021 is read from a chart
text: The FY2021 figure comes from ICE's FY2019–FY2024 removals bar chart in the FY2024 annual report (Figure 23), which labels each bar. ICE's own FY2021 annual-report PDF could not be retrieved. The other five bars in that chart match the figures printed in text elsewhere in ICE's documents.

title: From May 12, 2023, Border Patrol expedited removals flown by ICE Air are included
text: ICE's glossary: as of May 12, 2023, people processed for expedited removal and turned over from Border Patrol to ICE for removal via ICE Air are also counted as ICE removals.

title: FY2025 comes from ICE's budget submission and is preliminary
text: No ICE annual report or locked statistics file for FY2025 has been published. The figure is ICE's reported result for the measure 'total number of aliens returned and removed' in its FY2027 budget overview (a DHS document). The same table reports FY2024 as 271,484, identical to the annual report. Marked preliminary because ICE has not confirmed it as locked and may restate it.
